To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dielectric and PL properties of Si/SiO _{2} systems depend on the excess silicon incorporated within the SiO _{2} matrix.

the photoluminescence of the silicon nanograins is closely related to the silicon excess and that the dielectric function of silicon nanograined silica is strongly modified with respect to that of pure silica.

(1) the excess silicon is the main parameter controlling the optical properties of the system; (2) the dielectric function of silicon nanoparticles is similar to that of bulk silicon, except for the energy range where the interband transitions occur; (3) the PL properties are governed by the excess of silicon incorporated within silica.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the preparation of silicon nanoparticles embedded within a transparent silica matrix, which is suitable for use in the fabrication of optical devices.
the study of the dielectric properties of silicon nanoparticles in order to correlate the PL properties to the dielectric properties.
the optical properties of a silicon nanograins/silica matrix composite material and the correlation with its visible photoluminescent properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PL properties of silicon nanoparticles are governed by the silicon excess in the matrix and that the PL intensity and the energy of the PL peak can be controlled by the amount of silicon incorporated in the silica matrix.
the PL properties are strongly related to the excess silicon incorporated in the silica matrix.
the PL efficiency of silicon nanograin embedded systems is governed by the amount of excess silicon incorporated within the matrix and that the PL energy is governed by the size of the inclusions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PL efficiency and the energy of the PL emission are governed by the rate and size of the silicon nanograins.

the PL of the silicon nanograins is due to the presence of a high density of surface states and/or defects at the grain boundary, which act as trapping centres and recombination centres for the photogenerated carriers.
the PL efficiency is directly proportional to the silicon concentration, and the PL peak energy is inversely proportional to it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PL properties of silicon nanograined systems can be tailored by varying the silicon concentration in a silica matrix, which can be done by changing the sputtering time.
the ES technique is able to give a clear insight into the optical and structural properties of silicon nanograined films.
the ES approach is a very useful tool for the analysis of photoluminescence systems, and that this technique is very promising for the characterization and optimization of photoluminescing systems.
